quests.sentence: Yes I would love to come
quests.correctAnswer: Yes, I would love to come.
quests.hint: A short word like 'yes' at the start needs to be set apart before the main thought begins.
quests.explanation: An introductory word such as 'yes' or 'no' is followed by a comma to separate it from the sentence that follows.

quests.sentence: No I have not seen your umbrella
quests.correctAnswer: No, I have not seen your umbrella.
quests.hint: 'No' is standing alone at the start, announcing the main sentence to come.
quests.explanation: Just like 'yes,' the introductory word 'no' is followed by a comma before the rest of the sentence.

quests.sentence: Actually I already finished the report
quests.correctAnswer: Actually, I already finished the report.
quests.hint: Words like 'actually' or 'honestly' work the same way as 'yes' and 'no' at the start of a sentence.
quests.explanation: An introductory word that adds tone, such as 'actually,' is separated from the main sentence with a comma.

quests.sentence: Yesterday we visited my grandmother
quests.correctAnswer: Yesterday, we visited my grandmother.
quests.hint: A time word opens this sentence before the main action starts.
quests.explanation: An introductory time expression like 'yesterday' is set off with a comma before the main clause.

quests.sentence: Every morning he walks his dog around the block
quests.correctAnswer: Every morning, he walks his dog around the block.
quests.hint: This sentence opens with a phrase describing when something happens, not the subject yet.
quests.explanation: A time phrase that opens a sentence, such as 'every morning,' needs a comma before the main idea continues.

quests.sentence: Later tonight we will watch the fireworks
quests.correctAnswer: Later tonight, we will watch the fireworks.
quests.hint: Find the point where the time phrase ends and the subject of the sentence begins.
quests.explanation: Even a two-word time phrase like 'later tonight' is followed by a comma when it opens the sentence.

quests.sentence: In the morning the kitchen smells like fresh coffee
quests.correctAnswer: In the morning, the kitchen smells like fresh coffee.
quests.hint: This sentence begins with where or when something happens, before naming what happens.
quests.explanation: An introductory prepositional phrase like 'in the morning' is followed by a comma before the main sentence.

quests.sentence: After the game the team celebrated at the diner
quests.correctAnswer: After the game, the team celebrated at the diner.
quests.hint: The phrase 'after the game' sets the scene before telling us what actually happened.
quests.explanation: A phrase that tells when something happens, placed at the start of a sentence, is separated by a comma.

quests.sentence: Without a map we quickly got lost downtown
quests.correctAnswer: Without a map, we quickly got lost downtown.
quests.hint: The opening phrase explains a condition before the main event of the sentence.
quests.explanation: An introductory phrase describing a condition, like 'without a map,' takes a comma before the rest of the sentence.

quests.sentence: Suddenly the lights went out
quests.correctAnswer: Suddenly, the lights went out.
quests.hint: A single adverb opens the sentence to describe how something happened.
quests.explanation: An introductory adverb such as 'suddenly' is followed by a comma before the main clause.

quests.sentence: Fortunately no one was hurt in the accident
quests.correctAnswer: Fortunately, no one was hurt in the accident.
quests.hint: This adverb shows the writer's attitude about what follows, right from the first word.
quests.explanation: Attitude adverbs like 'fortunately' at the start of a sentence are set off with a comma.

quests.sentence: Meanwhile the rest of the class kept working quietly
quests.correctAnswer: Meanwhile, the rest of the class kept working quietly.
quests.hint: This word connects to something happening at the same time, and it opens the sentence.
quests.explanation: Transition adverbs like 'meanwhile' that begin a sentence are followed by a comma.

quests.sentence: Honestly I think we should leave earlier next time
quests.correctAnswer: Honestly, I think we should leave earlier next time.
quests.hint: This opening word is the same type you've seen before, just in a new situation.
quests.explanation: The introductory word 'honestly' still takes a comma before the main sentence, no matter the topic.

quests.sentence: Next weekend my cousins are visiting from out of town
quests.correctAnswer: Next weekend, my cousins are visiting from out of town.
quests.hint: This is another time expression opening the sentence, like ones you've punctuated before.
quests.explanation: An introductory time phrase such as 'next weekend' is followed by a comma before the subject appears.

quests.sentence: Because of the storm the flight was delayed for hours
quests.correctAnswer: Because of the storm, the flight was delayed for hours.
quests.hint: This phrase explains a cause before the main result is stated.
quests.explanation: An introductory phrase that gives a reason, like 'because of the storm,' is followed by a comma.

quests.sentence: Before you leave could you turn off the lights
quests.correctAnswer: Before you leave, could you turn off the lights?
quests.hint: This sentence starts with a phrase that sets a condition, and then it asks something.
quests.explanation: The introductory phrase needs a comma, and because the sentence is a request phrased as a question, it also needs a question mark.

quests.sentence: After the meeting are we still getting lunch
quests.correctAnswer: After the meeting, are we still getting lunch?
quests.hint: Look for the same two things as before: where the introductory phrase ends, and whether the sentence is asking.
quests.explanation: A comma follows the introductory time phrase, and since the sentence inverts the verb and subject to ask something, it ends with a question mark.

quests.sentence: Honestly do you think this plan will work
quests.correctAnswer: Honestly, do you think this plan will work?
quests.hint: The opening word signals tone, and the rest of the sentence signals purpose.
quests.explanation: The introductory word 'honestly' takes a comma, and the question format at the end needs a question mark.

quests.sentence: Finally we made it to the top of the mountain
quests.correctAnswer: Finally, we made it to the top of the mountain!
quests.hint: The opening word suggests relief, and the achievement described deserves more than a calm period.
quests.explanation: The introductory adverb 'finally' takes a comma, and the sense of achievement calls for an exclamation mark.

quests.sentence: Without any warning the fire alarm went off
quests.correctAnswer: Without any warning, the fire alarm went off!
quests.hint: An introductory phrase opens the sentence, and the sudden event that follows carries real intensity.
quests.explanation: The introductory phrase needs a comma, and the surprising, urgent event is marked with an exclamation point.

quests.sentence: At long last the package finally arrived
quests.correctAnswer: At long last, the package finally arrived!
quests.hint: This phrase builds anticipation before revealing the exciting result.
quests.explanation: The introductory phrase 'at long last' is followed by a comma, and the excitement of the outcome takes an exclamation mark.

quests.sentence: Before the trip we packed snacks water and sunscreen
quests.correctAnswer: Before the trip, we packed snacks, water, and sunscreen.
quests.hint: This sentence has both an opening phrase and a list at the end - handle each part separately.
quests.explanation: The introductory phrase takes a comma, and the three listed items each get separated by commas as well.

quests.sentence: During the sale we bought shoes jackets and gloves
quests.correctAnswer: During the sale, we bought shoes, jackets, and gloves.
quests.hint: Look for two separate comma jobs happening in the same sentence.
quests.explanation: A comma follows the introductory phrase 'during the sale,' and additional commas separate each item in the list.

quests.sentence: On the way home we stopped for gas food and coffee
quests.correctAnswer: On the way home, we stopped for gas, food, and coffee.
quests.hint: The sentence opens with where the action happens, then names several things in a row.
quests.explanation: The introductory phrase needs a comma, and the series of three stops needs commas between each item.

quests.sentence: Honestly I dont think we have enough time
quests.correctAnswer: Honestly, I don't think we have enough time.
quests.hint: This sentence needs both an introductory comma and a fix to a shortened word.
quests.explanation: The introductory word 'honestly' takes a comma, and 'don't' needs an apostrophe for the missing letter.

quests.sentence: After the storm we werent sure the roof was safe
quests.correctAnswer: After the storm, we weren't sure the roof was safe.
quests.hint: Two punctuation marks are missing here - one after the opening phrase, one inside a shortened word.
quests.explanation: The introductory phrase 'after the storm' needs a comma, and 'weren't' needs an apostrophe for 'were not.'

quests.sentence: Suddenly it wasnt clear who was in charge
quests.correctAnswer: Suddenly, it wasn't clear who was in charge.
quests.hint: Check the start of the sentence and the shortened word in the middle.
quests.explanation: The introductory adverb 'suddenly' is followed by a comma, and 'wasn't' needs an apostrophe for 'was not.'

quests.sentence: Before you go could you grab your keys wallet and phone
quests.correctAnswer: Before you go, could you grab your keys, wallet, and phone?
quests.hint: This message combines an opening phrase, a list, and a question all in one sentence.
quests.explanation: The introductory phrase takes a comma, the three items in the list are separated by commas, and the request phrased as a question ends with a question mark.

quests.sentence: Actually I dont think the meeting has started yet
quests.correctAnswer: Actually, I don't think the meeting has started yet.
quests.hint: This sentence needs an introductory comma and a fix to a contraction, without any question or exclamation.
quests.explanation: The introductory word 'actually' takes a comma, and 'don't' needs its apostrophe, while the calm statement still ends with a period.

quests.sentence: Finally we wont have to wait any longer
quests.correctAnswer: Finally, we won't have to wait any longer!
quests.hint: This message needs an opening comma, a fixed contraction, and an end mark that matches genuine relief.
quests.explanation: The introductory word 'finally' takes a comma, 'won't' needs an apostrophe, and the relief expressed calls for an exclamation mark.
